summary: John Hurrell Crook worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Southampton, Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe, and with Sheng Yen. He taught at Bristol (~1963–1995) and held a fellowship at CASBS (~1968–1969).

John J. Holder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies and studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

John J. Makransky specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, among others, and taught as a professor of comparative theology and Buddhist studies at Boston College (attested 1996–2007).

John James Jones was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Aberystwyth University (~1912–1916). He served as Deputy-Keeper of the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales (~1926–1957).

John Jorgensen is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA from the Australian National University under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner, and held posts at ANU, Griffith University, and La Trobe University.

John Kieschnick is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) before joining Stanford University (~2011) as the Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Professor of Buddhist Studies.

John Lane Bell is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford (~1963–1968). He held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1968–1989), the University of Western Ontario (~1989), and the National University of Singapore.

John Lockwood Kipling worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He taught at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (~1865–1875), was Principal of the National College of Arts (1875–1893), and served as Curator of Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

John M. Koller specialized in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles A. Moore, and George T. Artola, and served as a philosophy professor at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

John M. Rosenfield was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and art history. He earned a PhD from Harvard under Benjamin Rowland, later serving there as Professor (1965–1991) and Director of the Harvard Art Museums (~1982–1990).

John Marshall worked in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and the British School at Athens under Arthur John Evans, and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1902–1931).
John Marston is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington in 1997 and held a post at El Colegio de México.

John Muir was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Glasgow, East India Company College, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1844), and held a post at Edinburgh.

John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (~1968–1987), Lopon Tenzin Namdak (~1971), and Namkhai Norbu (~1976).

John Nemec is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn, under teachers including Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher. He is Associate Professor of Indian Religions and South Asian Studies at Virginia.

John Niemeyer Findlay was a philosopher who studied at Pretoria, Oxford, and Graz. His main posts included the University of Pretoria (~1927–1934), King's College London (~1951–1966), Yale University (~1970–1972), and Boston University (~1972–1987).

John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London (1959–1999).

John P. Keenan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, was a fellow at Nanzan University (1983–1986), and became Professor Emeritus of Religion at Middlebury College.

John Peile was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge and under Theodor Benfey. He served at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1860–1910), as Cambridge Reader of Comparative Philology (1884–1891), and as president of Newnham College (~1890–1909).
John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams and held a post as Professor at the University of Madras.
